svg.title: Home Lab Workshop: equipment and connection reference
svg.desc: Six generic teaching diagrams show router, switch, server, rack, radio and cable paths. Port counts match the simulator.
svg.text: Precise, scalable teaching diagrams · 3840 × 2160 canvas · Generic equipment, not manufacturer replicas

g.text: The router: an exit to other networks
LAN2 can be a separate routed subnet.
DHCP lends addresses. DNS resolves names.
A router connects IP networks; a switch connects local frames.
The switch: a local frame sorter
Six copper ports in this teaching model: 1 Gb/s each.
One SFP+ slot: matching 10 Gb/s optics or DAC.
PoE can power the access point through its copper link.
Cables, adapters and endpoints all limit performance.
The server: a physical home for VMs
Four 1 TB drives in RAID 10 → about 2 TB usable.
AM4 CPU + DDR4 UDIMM + matching NIC.
RAID helps availability. A separate backup helps recovery.
Disconnect power before fitting internal components.
Use rails or a rated shelf.
Heavy UPS low in the rack.
Wireless still needs a wired road
Join Wi-Fi, then obtain an IP address.
AP uplink carries data. Compatible PoE can carry power.
Associated with Wi-Fi does not mean Internet-ready.
Check power → link → IP → route → DNS → service.
A physical plug can fit while IP settings are wrong.
Pulsing data is an illustration, not a speed measurement.

svg.text: Match the simulator’s port labels and validation rules. Use the operating panel for interactive plugs, power and status.
